variables.H: number of bridges (switches) on the path = hop_count - 1
variables.t_sync_err: 1 us (single worst-case budget for network time error)

notes: Each bridge adds exactly one CQF cycle of latency (arrive in cycle n, leave in cycle n+1).
An additional cycle accounts for worst-case alignment at the source to the next transmit cycle (offset set to 0).
Propagation is counted per link (hop_count links including first source->switch and last switch->destination).
Switching delay is counted per bridge.
Time synchronization error is included as a single additive worst-case budget; guard bands are assumed to prevent extra cycle slips.
Serialization is computed from payload bytes only at 100 Mb/s (0.08 us per byte).

missing_inputs: Exact per-port gate phase/offsets and guard band sizes
Full Ethernet overhead per frame (preamble, SFD, IFG, L2 header/trailer)
Verification of per-cycle load per egress port to guarantee no cycle slip under CQF

all_parameters_used.queue_selection: alternate odd/even cycles (7 on odd, 6 on even)

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = H * (T + t_prop + t_ser + E) + S * t_sw

definitions.H: number of hops (links) in the given route
definitions.S: number of switches on the path (S = H - 1)
definitions.t_ser: serialization time per link = payload_bytes * 8 / bandwidth; here = bytes * 0.08 us at 100 Mbps
definitions.E: time synchronization error per hop (1 us)

WCD_calculation.hypercycle_computation: LCM of all cycle durations across all hops; all are 50 us, so Hypercycle = 50 us
WCD_calculation.offset_assignment: All flows have source offset = 0 us

missing_inputs: CQF typically requires cycle_time >= max_frame_serialization_time per egress. Here, many frames have t_ser > 50 us at 100 Mbps. I assumed frames can serialize across cycle boundaries and accounted for full serialization time per hop; no extra cycle slips due to overlength were added.

No per-port TT load or gate schedule/window sizes were provided. I assumed CQF double-buffering for TT with exclusive use of queues 7/6 and sufficient capacity per cycle to avoid multi-cycle backlogs beyond the single-cycle CQF wait per hop.
Ethernet L2 overhead (preamble, SFD, IFG, headers, FCS) was not specified. I used payload size only for t_ser; adding L2 overhead would increase WCD slightly.
Treatment of time synchronization error (1 us) was not specified (per hop vs. end-to-end). I added 1 us per hop.
End stations' CQF behavior was not explicitly stated. I assumed end stations also use CQF gating (thus one CQF cycle wait at the source egress).

cqf.policy: arrivals in cycle k transmit in cycle k+1 on each egress

assumptions: All TT flows use PCP 7 and the CQF two-queue pair (6 even, 7 odd) on every bridge egress they traverse.
Network-wide cycles are aligned; a frame that arrives during cycle k is forwarded in cycle k+1 at each bridge.
End stations/talkers are synchronized (offset set to 0) and do not add an extra CQF cycle beyond the bridge pipeline.
Serialization time is assumed to be budgeted inside the transmitting cycle (CQF dimensioning) and not added explicitly to WCD due to missing L2 overhead details.
all_parameters_used.WCD_equation: WCD (µs) = S*C + Hc*Tp + S*Ts + T_sync, where S = number of switches on the route, Hc = hop_count (links), C = cycle_duration_us, Tp = propagation_delay_us_per_link, Ts = switching_delay_us_per_switch, T_sync = time_synchronization_error_us

WCD_calculation.method: CQF per-bridge pipeline + fixed propagation and switching delays + one-time sync error

definitions.L: Number of links (hop_count from the route)

assumptions: Each switch egress introduces exactly one CQF cycle of residence (one-cycle forwarding).

Within-cycle serialization behind other TT frames is accounted for by the per-link serialization time term; no extra cycles are added.
Only payload bytes are considered for serialization (no L2 overhead modeled).

No per-cycle over-subscription/backlog; all TT frames assigned to a cycle fit within that cycle on each egress

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = N_sw * (T_cycle + t_sw + 2*epsilon) + N_links * t_prop

symbols.epsilon: time sync error bound (us) per hop (accounted as 2*epsilon per switch)
symbols.N_sw: number of switches on the path (hop_count - 1)
symbols.N_links: number of links on the path (hop_count)

missing_inputs: 802.1Qch feasibility requires max frame transmission time <= cycle time. At 100 Mbps, many payloads exceed 50 us (e.g., 809 B => 64.72 us), so per IEEE 802.1Qch a single cycle cannot hold such frames without preemption or longer cycles. The problem statement does not specify frame preemption (802.1Qbu/802.3br) or larger cycles.
Exact L2 overhead (headers, IFG, preamble, FCS) is unspecified; WCD above omits serialization time entirely under CQF-per-hop-equals-one-cycle modeling.
Guard band or gate open/close advance/retard relative to epsilon is unspecified; we modeled timing uncertainty as 2*epsilon per switch.
Whether end stations implement CQF is not explicitly stated; we assumed only bridges (switches) implement CQF.

One time synchronization error term e=1 us added end-to-end.

variables.L/C: serialization time = payload_bytes * 0.08 us at 100 Mbps

Exact CQF Gate Control List alignment (which of queues 6/7 transmits in even/odd cycles at each port) and any guard bands.
Admission control/schedulability proof for each port (ensuring all frames from cycle k finish within cycle k+1 transmit window).
Any per-flow shaping/jitter at sources and whether fragmentation of application payloads into multiple Ethernet frames is allowed.

all_parameters_used.cqf_behavior: Receive in cycle n, transmit in cycle n+1; even cycles transmit queue 7, odd cycles transmit queue 6
all_parameters_used.serialization_time_formula: t_tx_us = payload_bytes * 8 / (bandwidth_Mbps * 1e6) * 1e6 = payload_bytes * 0.08 us at 100 Mb/s

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = H*C + t_tx_last + t_prop_last
WCD_calculation.explanation: With CQF (802.1Qch), each hop contributes exactly one cycle of latency (frame received in cycle n, forwarded in cycle n+1). All intra-network serialization, switching and earlier-link propagation are absorbed within those cycles and do not add cycles. The final delivery to the receiver happens during the last hop’s transmit cycle, so the residual time to complete reception after the start of the last cycle is the last-link serialization plus its propagation.
notes: Even-cycle transmit queue = 7, odd-cycle transmit queue = 6; first transmit occurs in cycle 1 (queue 6) because offset=0 aligns with cycle 0 arrival.

Switching delay (1 us) and earlier-link propagation (1 us per hop) are small relative to C=50 us and do not increase the number of cycles; they are contained inside the per-hop cycle budgets. Only the last-link propagation is added explicitly.
All links are 100 Mb/s; serialization time t_tx_last = payload_B * 0.08 us.

CQF.rule: frames that arrive in cycle k are transmitted in cycle k+1, one hop per cycle; odd cycles use Q7, even cycles use Q6

assumptions: CQF adds exactly one cycle T on every relay hop (each switch) because frames that arrive in cycle k transmit in cycle k+1
Source offset is 0 so the first transmission can start at the beginning of cycle 0 (no initial cycle wait at the source NIC)
Cut-through reduces switch processing to the fixed 1 us given; no store-and-forward delay beyond CQF buffering
Per-hop propagation (1 us) is incurred on every link
Time sync error 1 us is budgeted as a guard of 2e per relay (before-close and after-open), i.e., 2 us per switch (conservative)
Serialization adds once at the source; later egress serializations are contained within the CQF cycle budget already counted
WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = t_ser_src + H*t_prop + (H-1)*(t_sw + T + 2*e)

variables.H: hop_count (number of links in the given route)
variables.t_ser_src: payload_bytes * 8 / bandwidth = payload_bytes * 0.08 us at 100 Mb/s
variables.e: time synchronization error = 1 us (guard per relay = 2e)

missing_inputs: Exact Ethernet overhead per frame (L2 header, preamble, IFG) to refine serialization time
Exact CQF gate open/close window within each cycle (we conservatively treated one full cycle per relay)
Confirmation of guard sizing (we used 2*e per relay); some deployments may use e per relay

Feasibility note: at 100 Mb/s and T=50 us, max serializable bytes within one cycle is ~625 B; several payloads exceed this, which would require either a longer cycle, smaller frames, or an implementation that allows entire-cycle gates and sufficient windowing — we computed WCDs nevertheless per the stated equation

interpretation.H_i: Number of links on the given route (equals provided hop_count)
interpretation.num_bridges: H_i - 1 (each intermediate switch adds one CQF cycle of residence)
interpretation.CQF: One-cycle per bridge (receive in cycle N, transmit in N+1). Q7 transmits on odd cycles; Q6 transmits on even cycles.
interpretation.sync_margin: 2*e per bridge to cover neighbor cycle skew in worst case

missing_inputs: Exact per-hop synchronization safety margin required by CQF (assumed 2*e per bridge)

all_parameters_used.queue_selection_rule: At egress index i along a flow's path, transmissions occur in cycle numbers c = i + n * (period_us / cycle_duration_us). If c is odd, queue 7; if c is even, queue 6.
all_parameters_used.hypercycle_derivation: LCM of cycle counts per period: periods {1000, 2500, 5000} µs with cycle 50 µs => cycles {20, 50, 100}; LCM = 100 cycles => 5000 µs.

WCD_calculation.equation: For flow f with hop_count h, cycle T_c, per-link propagation t_p, per-switch delay t_sw, link rate R, payload size S_f (bytes), and interference set I(p) at each egress port p on the path: WCD_f = h*T_c + h*t_p + (h-1)*t_sw + (S_f*8/R) + Σ_{p on path} Σ_{g in I(p)} (S_g*8/R). Here I(p) contains flows that share port p and transmit in the same cycle as f at p within the Hypercycle (worst-case, f is transmitted last in its cycle).
WCD_calculation.collision_condition: Two flows f and g collide at a shared egress p if there exists a cycle c in [1, Hypercycle_cycles] such that c ≡ i_f (mod P_f) and c ≡ i_g (mod P_g), where i_f is f's egress index at port p (1-based along its path), and P_f = period_us(f)/T_c (in cycles).

missing_inputs: Exact on-wire frame size (L2 overhead, preamble, IFG). Assumed payload bytes == transmitted bytes.
Exact CQF gate window sizes and guard bands per egress.
Ordering policy among TT frames within the same transmit cycle at an egress. Assumed worst-case: the target frame transmits last among co-scheduled frames of same cycle.
Whether time synchronization error should be added as extra delay margin. Not added to WCD; assumed covered by CQF one-cycle per hop bound.
Whether preemption (802.1Qbu/802.3br) is enabled. Assumed not used; only TT traffic occupies queues 6/7.

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = S*C + S*TSE + S*Switching + E*Prop + E*t_tx

variables.t_tx: serialization time per link = payload_bytes * 8 / (bandwidth_Mbps * 1e6) seconds, expressed in microseconds; here, t_tx (us) = payload_bytes * 0.08

missing_inputs: Exact egress gate schedules (open/close times) per port/class to verify that total serialized data per cycle does not exceed the transmit window.
Definition of whether end-stations (nodes) implement CQF egress gating; here assumed only bridges enforce CQF.
Frame format overheads (preamble, SFD, MAC header, VLAN tag, FCS, IFG); serialization modeled with payload bytes only.

Policy for t_tx relative to CQF cycle: several payloads exceed 625 B, which cannot fully serialize within a 50 us cycle at 100 Mb/s; without fragmentation or longer cycles, such frames are unschedulable under strict CQF one-cycle transmit windows.
Clarification of whether time synchronization error (1 us) should be accounted once per switch egress or per link in the WCD bound.

all_parameters_used.cycle_parity_rule: Even cycle: TX queue 6, RX into queue 7; Odd cycle: TX queue 7, RX into queue 6

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = t_ser_src + n_sw*C + n_links*D_prop + n_sw*D_sw + SyncErr

variables.t_ser_src: payload_B * 8 / (bandwidth_Mbps * 1e6) seconds = payload_B * 0.08 microseconds at 100 Mbps
variables.n_sw: number of switches traversed along the route (excluding end systems)
variables.C: CQF cycle duration (50 us), one cycle per switch hop
variables.n_links: number of links along the route (equals given hop_count)
variables.SyncErr: time synchronization error budget (1 us, added once)

assumptions: Offsets at sources are 0 us and aligned to the start of a TX window; no additional initial cycle wait
CQF is feasible on every port (no transmit window overrun); i.e., per-cycle TT load is admissible
All TT flows share PCP=7, thus share the same CQF two-queue set (6/7) per port; ordering within a TX window does not add cycle delays beyond 1 cycle per hop

missing_inputs: Per-frame overheads (preamble, SFD, VLAN tag, FCS, IFG) to refine serialization time
Exact CQF guard band configuration and gating offsets at each port
Confirmation that a 50 us TX window is valid at 100 Mbps for the given maximum payload sizes (several frames exceed 50 us serialization at 100 Mbps)
Per-port TT window share and schedule (to bound possible multi-cycle spillover under contention)
Any shaping/jitter constraints beyond CQF (e.g., TAS schedules) that could alter per-hop cycle usage

cqf_parameters.cqf_pipeline_rule: At most one CQF cycle of waiting per bridge hop (egress), alternating queues per cycle: odd->Q7, even->Q6

global.cqf_pipeline_rule: Each bridge adds exactly one CQF cycle of queuing (frame arriving in cycle n transmits in cycle n+1 at that bridge).

sw_0_0.P1.F2: Q6 (even hop index at that bridge)
sw_0_0.P1.F7: Q7 (odd hop index at that bridge)

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = H*C + H*d_prop + (H-1)*d_sw + d_sync

variables.d_sw: switching delay per switch (1 us, cut-through)
variables.d_sync: time synchronization error margin (1 us, applied once)

notes: CQF relays a frame to the next hop in the next cycle; using H*C is a safe upper bound on cycle-based latency.
Propagation and switching delays are added deterministically; the sync error is included once as a margin.
Serialization delay is not included because exact L2 frame size (incl. headers/preamble/IFG) is unspecified.

Confirmation that end stations (nodes) use CQF double-buffering; egress queue indices on nodes are not enumerated.
Validation that each frame fits within a 50 us transmission window at 100 Mbps (some given payloads would exceed 50 us if treated as single frames).
Clarification whether switching delay should be counted in addition to CQF cycle latency for cut-through operation (assumed yes, as fixed 1 us per switch).

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD_f = (H_f + Σ_extra_cycles_over_egress_ports_f) * T + (H_f * d_prop) + ((H_f - 1) * d_sw) + d_sync

terms.H_f: hop_count (number of links) for flow f from given route
terms.Σ_extra_cycles_over_egress_ports_f: sum over all egress ports on f's path of (ceil(total_bytes_transmitted_in_worst_aligned_cycle / bytes_per_cycle) - 1), computed with offset=0 and CQF 1-cycle-per-hop alignment
terms.d_sw: switching delay per bridge hop = 1 µs
terms.d_sync: time synchronization error allowance = 1 µs (applied once end-to-end)

WCD_calculation.alignment_method: For each shared egress port, compute each flow's transmit cycle index at that port as (hop_index_along_path) modulo (period_in_cycles), with periods 1000/50=20, 2500/50=50, 5000/50=100. Identify cycles within the 100-cycle hypercycle where flows coincide; sum payloads in those cycles to get worst per-cycle backlog.

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = H*C + L*P + H*S + ε

variable_definitions.H: number of CQF hops (number of switches on the path) = hop_count - 1
variable_definitions.L: number of links on the path = hop_count
variable_definitions.ε: time synchronization error margin (µs) applied once end-to-end

assumptions: Two-queue CQF pipeline: a frame received in cycle k is transmitted in cycle k+1 at every switch (1 cycle per switch).
No output port is shared by multiple TT flows at PCP=7 in this dataset; thus no additional non-preemption/multiplexing term.
Frame serialization time is absorbed within the CQF cycle budget (i.e., frames fit into the transmit window), hence not added explicitly to WCD.

missing_inputs: Exact gate control list (GCL) per egress port (open/close times and guard bands).
Clarification whether L1/L2 overhead must be added to payload size for serialization time, and whether serialization shall be included in WCD for CQF.
Confirmation that end stations do not implement CQF gating (source is free-running and first CQF stage is the first switch).
Validation that each frame fits into a 50 µs transmit window at 100 Mbps; some payloads would exceed 50 µs if serialization is considered.

all_parameters_used.cqf_mode: Dual-queue even/odd (IEEE 802.1Qch), PCP=7 mapped to Q7/Q6, cut-through
assumptions: All TT frames fit within a single CQF transmit window per hop (no multi-cycle spillover at any egress).
No frame preemption is used; one class (PCP=7) mapped to the CQF TT queue pair only.
Serialization time is computed from payload only (no additional L2 overhead applied).
WCD measured until the last bit is received at the destination end station.
Per-hop CQF queuing contributes at most one full cycle per switching stage; an additional cycle is counted at the source stage.

WCD_calculation.equation: Let N_links = hop_count; N_sw = number of switches on path = hop_count - 1; ser_per_link_us = payload_bytes * 8 / (100 Mbps) = payload_bytes * 0.08 us. Then WCD = (N_sw + 1)*T_c + N_links*(prop_delay) + N_sw*(switching_delay) + N_links*(ser_per_link_us) + (N_sw + 1)*(sync_error). With T_c=50us, prop_delay=1us/link, switching_delay=1us/switch, sync_error=1us per stage.

missing_inputs: Ethernet L2 overhead per frame (headers, FCS, preamble, IFG) to include in serialization time.
Exact CQF gate phase/offset per egress port (to prove or tighten the +1 cycle at source and per-hop alignment).
Guard band or frame preemption configuration (could affect effective serialization within a cycle).
Per-port TT load per cycle to exclude multi-cycle spillover with certainty.

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = s_first + (n_sw_egress * ceil(s/C) * C) + (hop_count * prop) + (n_sw_egress * sw) + t_sync

definitions.s_first: Serialization time on the first (source->first switch) link = payload_B * 8 / bandwidth
definitions.n_sw_egress: Number of switch egresses along the path (equals number of switches on the path)
definitions.hop_count: Number of links in the route (from routing table)
definitions.t_sync: Global time synchronization error allowance (added once path-wide)
definitions.ceil(s/C): Number of transmit cycles needed per CQF-gated hop

missing_inputs: Exact GCL (gate control lists) per egress port, including transmit window durations and guard bands
Definition of full frame size (payload vs. payload + L2/L1 overhead); we treated payload bytes as frame size
Explicit rule for handling frames whose serialization exceeds one cycle in CQF (we used ceil(s/C) per gated hop)
Any per-flow launch-time offsets at sources beyond 0, and whether sources are themselves CQF-gated

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD_f = S_f*T + E_f*(L_f*8/C) + E_f*t_prop + S_f*t_sw + S_f*t_sync
notes: S_f = number of bridges (switches) on the path
E_f = number of links = hop_count from the route
L_f*8/C converted to microseconds equals L_f * 0.08 us at 100 Mbps
CQF adds one full cycle per bridge (receive in cycle n, transmit in n+1)

missing_inputs: Explicit statement whether talker egress uses CQF (would add +T at source); assumed no extra CQF cycle at endpoints

Per-port gate open times/guard bands and cycle utilization; assumed no cycle overrun/backlog

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD_f = (B_f + 1)*C + L_f*D_prop + B_f*D_sw + T_tx_lasthop_f + E_sync

variables.B_f: number of CQF-regulated bridges (switches) on flow f's path
variables.L_f: number of links on flow f's path
variables.D_sw: cut-through switching delay per bridge (1 µs)
variables.T_tx_lasthop_f: serialization time on the last hop for flow f = payload_bytes * 8 / 100e6 s
variables.E_sync: end-to-end time synchronization error budget (1 µs)
variables.Note: The (B_f + 1)*C term accounts for worst-case initial alignment (≤1 cycle at source) plus 1 cycle of CQF residence at each bridge.

missing_inputs: Exact CQF phase (which queue transmits in cycle 0) per egress; we assumed odd cycles TX=Q7, even cycles TX=Q6.
Confirmation whether end stations (nodes) implement CQF gating; we assumed worst-case initial 1-cycle alignment at the source and 1-cycle per bridge.
Per-port TT window sizes (or CQF cycle allocation per priority). Without this, intra-cycle serialization contention among multiple PCP=7 flows sharing a port cannot be bounded more tightly.
Frame overheads (L2 header, VLAN tag, FCS, preamble, IFG). We computed serialization using payload only; including overhead would slightly increase T_tx_lasthop.

Feasibility note: At 100 Mbps and 50 µs cycles, some payloads (e.g., 783 B) require >50 µs to serialize, which would overrun a single transmit window in strict CQF. A practical system would need a longer cycle or smaller frames.

cqf_parameters.assumed_phase_alignment: all egress ports share the same cycle boundaries

assumptions_and_CQF_model: Synchronous CQF across the network: each hop contributes one full cycle (C) residence time (frame arrives in collect phase k, departs in transmit phase k+1).
Cut-through switching is used; a fixed 1 µs switching delay per switch is added.
Propagation delay per link is 1 µs.
Serialization time is computed from payload only: t_ser = payload_bytes * 8 / 100e6 s = payload_bytes * 0.08 µs, applied once per flow at the first transmission.
All TT frames use PCP 7 and queues 7 (odd cycles) and 6 (even cycles).
No explicit guard band or gate offset is provided; global cycle boundaries are assumed aligned.
WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = H*C + H*t_prop + (H-1)*t_sw + t_ser, where H = hop_count (links), C = 50 µs, t_prop = 1 µs/link, t_sw = 1 µs/switch, t_ser = payload_bytes * 0.08 µs

missing_inputs: Exact CQF gate phase offsets per port (if any) and guard band configuration.
Confirmation whether end stations apply CQF at the NIC or only TAS (affects first-hop behavior).
Definition of whether serialization time should be accounted on every hop with CQF cut-through, or only once (we applied it once, at source).
Frame overheads (preamble, SFD, MAC headers, VLAN tag, FCS, IFG) not provided; t_ser was computed from payload bytes only.

With C=50 µs at 100 Mbps, several payloads exceed the per-cycle capacity (625 bytes/cycle). The network would require multi-cycle allocation or a larger cycle. Absent such details, the bound above assumes synchronous CQF with one-cycle-per-hop residence time and counts serialization once.

It is not stated whether frames may start transmission near a cycle boundary if they would finish after the boundary; analysis assumes standard CQF behavior with two queues alternating per cycle.

definitions.hop_count: Number of links in the given route (from the routing table).
definitions.t_tx: Serialization time per frame on a 100 Mb/s link, computed as payload_bytes * 8 / 100e6 seconds = 0.08 * payload_bytes (us). (Payload used as proxy for L2 frame size.)
definitions.e: Time synchronization error budget per hop = 1 us.
definitions.offset: Set to 0 us at every source as required.

Per-port gate phase alignment (I assumed globally aligned cycles across the network).
Guard band sizes and any additional CQF advance/delay configuration were not provided.
Use (or not) of frame preemption (802.1Qbu/802.3br). I assumed no preemption.
Admission control/sizing per cycle per port. I assumed cycles are sufficiently provisioned so that all scheduled TT frames fit the intended transmission cycle.
Interpretation of the 1 us time synchronization error: I applied 1 us per hop; if it is end-to-end, the WCDs would be slightly over-conservative.

Strict CQF typically requires frames to fit within the transmit window. I computed WCD assuming such frames are still admissible and the equation remains valid; otherwise, feasibility must be rechecked or cycle duration increased.

cqf_specific.gate_behavior: receive in cycle N, transmit in cycle N+1 on alternate buffer/queue

WCD_calculation.equation: For each flow f: WCD_f = t_ser_src(f) + S_f*(ceil(t_ser_src(f)/C)*C + t_sw) + L_f*t_prop + T_sync_margin

variable_definitions.t_ser_src(f): Serialization time at 100 Mb/s for flow f payload (Bytes*8/100e6) in microseconds
variable_definitions.S_f: Number of switches along f's path
variable_definitions.L_f: Number of links (edges) along f's path
variable_definitions.T_sync_margin: Global margin for time sync error (1 us, conservative single-shot)

assumptions: End stations generate TT frames at offset 0; switches implement CQF; end stations do not gate CQF (they only serialize the frame).
Per-hop CQF forwarding requires at least one full cycle; if frame serialization exceeds the cycle, ceil(t_ser/C) cycles are budgeted for that egress.
No additional backlog build-up within a cycle (i.e., TT scheduling per egress fits within allocated cycles); inter-flow interference is handled by CQF cycle separation.
Only payload size is used for serialization time (no L2/L1 overheads provided).
Cut-through switching delay is constant 1 us and independent of frame size.
notes: Some flows have t_ser > C (50 us). In strict CQF, C is typically chosen >= max serialization time; here we conservatively account for multi-cycle serialization by using ceil(t_ser/C) cycles per switch egress.
Time synchronization error (1 us) is included once as an end-to-end margin; its effect is bounded within the one-cycle-per-switch gating budget.

Confirmation whether end stations also implement CQF or Qbv gating
Validation of CQF feasibility where t_ser > cycle time (50 us); strict CQF typically requires cycle >= max t_ser

cqf_parameters.per_bridge_cycle_increment: 1 cycle per bridge (receive in cycle i, transmit in cycle i+1)

F1.contention_set_comment: All flows on a given egress port use PCP 7 mapped to the CQF pair {7 (odd), 6 (even)}. Under CQF, contention does not add variable delay; each bridge adds exactly one cycle.

F2.contention_set_comment: CQF fixes one-cycle per-bridge latency; sharing sw_3.P0 with F4 and F7 does not add queueing beyond that.

cqf_parameters.per_bridge_cycle_increment: 1 cycle per bridge (receive in cycle i, transmit in cycle i+1)

F3.contention_set_comment: F3 shares all egress ports with F6. Under CQF, both experience the same per-bridge 1-cycle latency.

cqf_parameters.per_bridge_cycle_increment: 1 cycle per bridge (receive in cycle i, transmit in cycle i+1)

F4.contention_set_comment: F4 shares sw_1.P4 with F7 and sw_3.P0 with F2 and F7; CQF keeps latency deterministic.

cqf_parameters.per_bridge_cycle_increment: 1 cycle per bridge (receive in cycle i, transmit in cycle i+1)

F5.contention_set_comment: F5 does not share egress ports with other listed flows; CQF still fixes 1-cycle per bridge.

cqf_parameters.per_bridge_cycle_increment: 1 cycle per bridge (receive in cycle i, transmit in cycle i+1)

F6.contention_set_comment: Duplicate of F3; identical path and CQF behavior.

cqf_parameters.per_bridge_cycle_increment: 1 cycle per bridge (receive in cycle i, transmit in cycle i+1)

F7.contention_set_comment: Duplicate of F4; identical path and CQF behavior.

WCD_calculation.equation_used: WCD = (B * Tc) + (N_links * t_prop) + (B * t_sw) + t_sync + (L_bytes * 8 / Bw)
WCD_calculation.notes: CQF enforces one full cycle per bridge. Source offset set to 0, so no additional initial cycle added. Serialization is included once (on the final egress) to account for last-bit arrival; contention does not add variable delay under CQF.

missing_inputs: Exact egress gate open duration per cycle and guard band sizing for CQF on each port
Whether end stations implement CQF two-queue gating identically to bridges (assumed yes)
Ethernet on-wire frame size (headers, VLAN tag, preamble/SFD, IFG); payload-only was assumed for serialization
Whether Frame Preemption (802.1Qbu/802.3br) is enabled; affects ability to fit large frames into a 50 µs window
Allocation of time-synchronization error to latency vs. guard band (assumed 1 µs added once end-to-end)

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = (h + 2) * T_c + h * t_prop + (h - 1) * t_sw + h * t_sync + t_ser, where t_ser = (payload_B * 8) / (R_bps) and R_bps = 100e6 bits/s (i.e., 100 bits/µs).

missing_inputs: Whether end stations (node0_*) implement CQF gating identically to bridges (assumed yes).
Exact CQF gate open/close times per port (assumed full-cycle windows with strict CQF pipeline: receive in cycle n, transmit in n+1).
Ethernet L2 overhead (preamble/SFD, MAC header, VLAN tag, FCS, IFG) not specified; serialization used payload only.
Exact treatment of time synchronization error within guard bands (applied as 1 µs per hop margin here).
Potential intra-cycle contention/backlog on shared egress ports not provided; assumed link utilization low enough that frames fit within their assigned cycle without spilling to additional cycles.

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD_i = H*C + H*d_prop + (H - 1)*d_sw + T_ser_i + epsilon_sync

variables.T_ser_i: serialization time of flow i payload at 100 Mbps (us) = payload_bytes * 8 / 100e6 = 0.08 * payload_bytes

assumptions: Two-queue CQF alternation (even: TX Q6, odd: TX Q7) with one-hop-per-cycle progression
Initial release at t=0; first transmission occurs in the subsequent transmit cycle (implicit one-cycle source hold)
No additional intra-cycle contention delay is added beyond the last-hop serialization time
No frame preemption; cut-through switching with fixed 1 us per switch

reason.notes_on_port_queues: At every egress port, TT frames with PCP=7 use queue 7 in odd cycles and queue 6 in even cycles (CQF two-queue alternation).
missing_inputs: Ethernet L2 overheads (preamble, SFD, IFG, headers) to compute full serialization time per frame; payload-only used here.
Per-port CQF gate phase (which queue transmits in cycle 0) to align exact cycle indices.
Confirmation whether intra-cycle contention (sum of same-priority frames in one transmit cycle) must be modeled; not included in the WCD above.

Feasibility with C=50 us: payloads of 690 B and 1045 B serialize to 55.2 us and 83.6 us at 100 Mbps, which do not fit a 50 us transmit window without preemption or larger cycle; if enforced strictly, configuration is infeasible and WCD would be undefined.

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD_f = H*T_c + H*t_prop + S*t_sw + t_sync + t_ser_last

variable_definitions.H: hop_count (number of links on the route)
variable_definitions.S: number of switches on the path = H - 1
variable_definitions.t_sw: cut-through switching delay per switch (1 us)
variable_definitions.t_sync: network time synchronization error margin (1 us total)
variable_definitions.t_ser_last: serialization time on last hop = payload_bytes*8 / (100 Mbps) = payload_bytes * 0.08 us

assumptions: End-stations (nodes) participate in CQF as the first CQF stage; each link transmission corresponds to one CQF stage.
All TT frames with PCP=7 map to the same CQF A/B buffer pair on each egress port (odd->queue 7, even->queue 6).
Cut-through switching prevents additional store-and-forward latency; only the configured 1 us switching delay is added per switch.
Only the last-hop serialization time contributes to WCD because upstream serialization overlaps with CQF cycle waiting.
Frame length equals the given payload size (no L2/L1 overheads modeled).
CQF gates are open for the full cycle (no additional guard-band loss modeled).
One global t_sync margin (1 us) is added to the end-to-end WCD to account for synchronization uncertainty across hops.

missing_inputs: Exact per-port GCL offsets and guard bands to verify cycle alignment and possible extra cycle slips
Whether end-stations implement CQF gating (assumed yes here)
L2/L1 overheads (MAC header, VLAN tag, preamble, IFG) for accurate serialization times
Policy for applying time synchronization error (per hop vs end-to-end margin)
Constraint that frame transmission time must fit within the CQF cycle (some payloads exceed 50 us at 100 Mbps)

all_parameters_used.arrival_rounding_rule: At each bridge i: transmit in cycle ceil((arrival_time + sync_error)/T) with two-queue alternation

CQF_equations_used: Per bridge i: c_i_base = ceil((t_{i-1} + sigma)/T), ts_i = c_i * T + Sw
t_i = ts_i + S + P (arrival at next node)

If K frames share the same egress and same activation (same queue): total serialization sum ΣS; required queue activations N = ceil(ΣS / T). For worst-case flow ordering, c_i_actual = c_i_base + 2*(N - 1) (two-queue alternation), ts_i = c_i_actual*T + Sw
End-to-end WCD = ts_H + S + P_last (after final egress transmission and last propagation)
assumptions: Offsets at all sources set to 0
No frame preemption; frames are serialized in full once started
Gate is open for the entire cycle for a given queue (Q7 in odd cycles, Q6 in even cycles)
If multiple frames exceed the per-cycle transmit budget, leftover frames wait until the next activation of the same queue (two cycles later)
Time sync error applied once per hop as worst-case positive offset before cycle rounding
No additional Ethernet overhead (headers, IFG, preamble) beyond payload for serialization time calculation (not provided)

missing_inputs: Exact mapping of queue-to-cycle polarity per port (we assumed Q7=odd, Q6=even as stated)
Exact guard band or gate close behaviors and whether transmission is allowed to extend past gate close
On-wire overheads (preamble, SFD, IFG, MAC headers, FCS) not provided; we used payload-only for serialization
Explicit per-port TT schedule/order within a cycle; we assumed worst-case ordering for WCD at shared egresses

WCD_calculation.equation: WCD = S * ceil((t_ser + t_prop + t_sw + t_sync)/C) * C + t_ser + t_prop

variables.S: number of switches on the path (here S=2 for all flows)
variables.t_ser: serialization time on the link = payload_B * 8 / 100e6 [s] = payload_B * 0.08 [us]
variables.t_prop: propagation delay per link (1 us), added once more for the final link
variables.t_sw: cut-through switching delay per switch (1 us), inside per-switch time budget
variables.t_sync: time synchronization error budget per hop (1 us), inside per-switch time budget

notes: ceil((t_ser + t_prop + t_sw + t_sync)/C) is the number of CQF cycles needed at each switch to safely forward the frame without cycle slip.
The first-switch budget includes the source->first-switch link serialization/propagation and the first switch processing.
The last-switch budget includes the inter-switch link serialization/propagation and the last switch processing.
The final hop (last switch -> destination) adds serialization and propagation outside any further CQF stage.
Initial waiting is 0 us because the talker offset is fixed to 0 as required.

missing_inputs: Exact per-port Gate Control List (GCL) phase/alignment; assumed globally in-phase CQF cycles.
Ethernet overheads (MAC header, VLAN tag, FCS, preamble, IFG); serialization time was computed from payload bytes only.
Whether end stations implement CQF gates; analysis assumes CQF cycles counted per switch (not at the talker NIC).
Any guard band durations; assumed negligible or folded into the cycle budget.
Exact TT window sizing per cycle; assumed full-cycle TT availability on queues 7/6.

At 100 Mbps, payloads of 1045 B and 1408 B imply serialization times of ~83.6 µs and ~112.6 µs, both > 50 µs. Without frame preemption or a larger T, exact CQF-compliant timing (and thus tighter WCD) cannot be guaranteed.

WCD_calculation.equation: Let T be the CQF cycle time. For each flow with constant serialization time S = payload_bytes * 8 / (bandwidth in bps). Define at each bridge j the time to fully receive the frame t_rx_end_j = S + prop_j + sw_j added to the time reference carried from the previous stage. The transmit start time at bridge j is t_tx_start_j = ceil(t_rx_end_j / T) * T. After transmitting across link j+1, the next stage’s receive-finish time is updated by adding S + prop_{j+1} + sw_{j+1} to t_tx_start_j. The final worst-case one-way latency is t_dest_finish = t_tx_start_last_bridge + S + prop_last_link + sync_margin.
